meta.topic: JVM, JDK & JRE — Java Platform Architecture
meta.session_title: Day 1 - Introduction to Java & Language Fundamentals
meta.pedagogy: Hands-on learning with step-by-step guidance. Each exercise builds on the previous. All concepts from the session are coded. Banking/finance examples used for context.

objectives: Understand the structure of a Java program, compile and run it, and understand the role of JVM/JDK/JRE.
prerequisites: IntelliJ IDEA (Community Edition) or VS Code with Java Extension
Git installed and GitHub account created

exercises.title: Your First Java Program — Hello, Software Engineer!
exercises.objective: Understand the structure of a Java program, compile and run it, and understand the role of JVM/JDK/JRE.
exercises.scenario: You just joined RoboBank's technology team as a fresher. Your first task: set up your Java environment and write a program that introduces you to the team.
instructions: Step 1: Open your IDE and create a new Java project called 'Day01_JavaFundamentals'
Step 2: Create a new Java class named 'HelloEngineer' inside the project's src folder
Step 3: Type (don't copy-paste!) the starter code below
Step 4: Run the program (Shift+F10 in IntelliJ, or F5 in VS Code)
Step 5: Open a terminal and locate the compiled .class file: it should be in 'out/' or 'build/' folder
Step 6: From the terminal, try: javac HelloEngineer.java → java HelloEngineer
Step 7: Modify the output to include YOUR name and YOUR city
Checkpoint: Can you explain to a classmate what javac does vs what java does?
exercises.expected_output:
Hello from RoboBank Tech Team!
I am: [Your Name]
Based in: [Your City]
Java version I'm using: 17.0.x

--- Java Platform Architecture ---
JDK  = JRE + Development Tools (javac, javadoc, jar)
JRE  = JVM + Standard Class Libraries
JVM  = Executes .class bytecode | Platform-specific
WORA = Write Once, Run Anywhere!
hints: If you get 'class not found': make sure the filename matches the class name exactly (case-sensitive!)
If you see a .class file in a folder — that's the bytecode! Open it in Notepad to see it's not readable — that's the JVM's job to understand it.
Each System.out.println() is one statement. Every statement ends with a semicolon.
reflection_questions: What is the difference between a .java file and a .class file?
Why can the same .class file run on both Windows and Linux?
What would happen if you renamed HelloEngineer.java to Hello.java without changing the class name?
exercises.debugging_task: Try removing the semicolon from one of the println statements and recompile. What error do you get? Read the error message carefully — what does it tell you?
